input: Convert /data/users.csv to a JSON array where each row becomes an object with the column headers as keys. Print the resulting JSON to stdout.

tool_calls:
which jq python3 python perl ruby node miller csvjson 2>&1; jq --version 2>&1; echo EXIT:$?
ls /usr/bin/ | tr '\n' ' ' | fold -w 150
echo
cat /etc/os-release 2>&1 | head

ls /usr/bin/ | tr '\n' '\n' | sort
echo "=== yq ==="; yq --version 2>&1; yq --help 2>&1 | head -n 100
echo "=== tomlq ==="; tomlq --help 2>&1 | head -n 20
echo "=== jq help ==="; jq --help 2>&1 | head -n 40
csv 2>&1 | head -n 100; echo "====EXIT:$?"; echo "---"; json 2>&1 | head -n 100; echo "====EXIT:$?"

csv headers /data/users.csv 2>&1
echo "---"
csv count /data/users.csv 2>&1
echo "---"
csv select --help 2>&1 | head -n 100
csv select 2>&1 | head -n 100
csv headers 2>&1 | head -n 100
echo "--- json ---"
json pretty 2>&1 | head -n 50
echo '{"a":1}' | json pretty 2>&1 | head -n 50
cat -A /data/users.csv
hexdump -C /data/users.csv
gawk --version 2>&1 | head
